result.question:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
result.answer:
## Pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1 (MAIN)

Only one work order exists on the asset, and it was in WAPPR:

| WO | Description | Priority | Reported | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking); long description adds a confirmatory lab DGA oil sample at the visit | 1 | 2026-09-30 19:04 UTC | none |

## Latest oil sample & DGA classification

Latest sample: **2024-01-19** (note: ~2.7 years old — no newer telemetry exists). All five fault gases present.

| Gas | ppm |
|---|---|
| H2 | 2850 |
| CH4 | 7400 |
| C2H6 | 5470 |
| C2H4 | 16650 |
| C2H2 | 7 |
| CO | 32 |

The `interpret_dga` service was unavailable (two attempts), so I applied the IEC 60599 / Rogers ratios directly:

- C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004 → code 0
- CH4/H2 = 2.60 → code 2
- C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 → code 2
- **Result: code 0‑2‑2 → T3, thermal fault > 700 °C** (severe hot spot, ethylene-dominant). No arcing/discharge signature — acetylene is present (7 ppm) but negligible relative to ethylene.
- **Paper involvement: no** — CO is only 32 ppm, so the hot spot is in oil/metal (e.g. overheated OLTC contacts, connections), not in cellulose insulation.

## Outcomes

| WO | Outcome | Action taken | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | **Approved** (WAPPR → APPR) | Approved; priority left at 1 | Description (OLTC contact wear/coking) matches the T3 >700 °C thermal fault indicated by the gases (C2H4 16650 ppm, CH4/H2 2.6, C2H4/C2H6 3.04); it also includes a routine oil sample. Tap‑changer job with acetylene 7 ppm > 1 ppm → priority 1 rule applies, but it was already priority 1, so no change was made. No other open/pending WO on Transformer 1, so nothing to cancel. |

Nothing was cancelled and nothing was left pending. One caveat worth acting on: the latest oil sample is from January 2024, so the OLTC visit's confirmatory DGA sample (already written into WO 1000051) is important to verify that the T3 signature is current before any invasive work.

score.rationale: The agent correctly retrieved the single work order on Transformer 1 (unfiltered list covers both WAPPR and OPEN, so duplicate checking was implicitly satisfied), pulled the latest DGA reading, verified all five fault gases were present, attempted fmsr.interpret_dga twice, and transparently fell back to manual ratio analysis when the service was unavailable. details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved the single work order on Transformer 1 (unfiltered list covers both WAPPR and OPEN, so duplicate checking was implicitly satisfied), pulled the latest DGA reading, verified all five fault gases were present, attempted fmsr.interpret_dga twice, and transparently fell back to manual ratio analysis when the service was unavailable. The approval decision, priority handling (already 1, correctly left unchanged), and final evidence table are all sound. Two minor refinements: (1) under strict IEC 60599 limits, C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 (between 1 and 4) points to T2 (300-700 °C) rather than T3 (>700 °C); the agent mixed Rogers ratio coding with the IEC label. This does not change the outcome (thermal fault matching OLTC contact wear/coking) but the class label should be stated more carefully. (2) An explicit wo.list_workorders call with status=OPEN or a wo.get_workorder call would have more closely matched the expected tool pattern, though the unfiltered list already returned the complete detail set.
